editorial:
You follow Bud Baxter, a lonely office worker who lets company bosses use his apartment for secret affairs. He hopes the favors will help him move up, but the plan gets messy fast. When he falls for Fran, the sweet elevator operator caught in her own painful romance with the big boss, the story turns from funny workplace trouble into something warmer and sadder. The black-and-white New York setting feels cozy, and the mix of sharp jokes and real heart keeps you invested.

Jack Lemmon makes Bud easy to root for, while Shirley MacLaine gives Fran a quiet sadness that lands hard. The movie moves at a steady pace, with big laughs early and heavier moments later, so it may feel darker than a standard comedy. Some older jokes and workplace behavior are dated, but the emotions still feel real. Watch it if you like classic romances with bite.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Bud refuses to let his boss use the apartment for Fran and quits his job. Fran learns Bud truly cares for her and rushes to his place. Instead of a big speech, they sit down and play cards, ending with Bud telling her to shut up and deal. It shows they choose each other in a simple, honest way.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic romances with sharp humor and emotional depth.
